Subject: Follow-up: FinBird continuous-batching & unit-econ confirmation

Hi Alyssa — great to meet today, thanks for the clear framing. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying asks so we can turn this into a tailored estimate and a short canary plan.

Recap from our call
- Primary workload: nightly enrichment pipeline (~continuous background calls) + interactive search augmentation for internal ops.
- Current product target: ~15 sustained QPS for background enrichment; interactive workload adds bursts to ~120 QPS for short windows.
- Self-reported token mix: prompts average ~420 tokens (user + system) and generated output ~380 tokens, so ~800 tokens per request on average.
- Desired cost target: you mentioned wanting to keep total model spend around a specific range — can you confirm target $/1M tokens? You said loosely $40–$60 but we want explicit confirmation.

Assumptions we'd like you to confirm
1) Monthly volume band: is 20M – 60M tokens/month the right range (based on the numbers you gave)? If not, please give a comfortable low/high.
2) Latency SLO: for interactive augmentation you're targeting P95 < 300ms, for enrichment you care more about throughput and steady-state cost rather than p95. Is that correct?
3) Continuous batching expectation: do you expect the enrichment calls to be steady (near constant throughout the day) or more diurnal with multi-hour peaks? Continuous batching has different cost profiles if traffic is truly uniform vs. spiky.

Our proposed next steps (pending your confirmation)
- We’ll produce a 3-line estimate showing per-1M-token unit cost across two modes (hosted continuous-batching and dedicated reserved capacity) and show expected monthly bill for low/typical/high.
- Provide a canary run proposal (2 weeks) with suggested batching and concurrency settings; we’ll include expected cost delta vs. no-batching.
- Share a short CSV template to capture exact token breakdowns (attached).

Attachments: workload_sample.csv (CSV), rdw-billing-estimate.xlsx (prototype)

Can you confirm the three assumptions above and the explicit target $/1M tokens you want us to hit? If $40–$60 is accurate, tell us the hard ceiling. Once confirmed we’ll send the estimate + canary config by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,

Thanks Rishi — good summary. Quick answers inline and a few clarifications.

On Jul 12, 2026, at 3:22 PM, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Monthly volume band: is 20M – 60M tokens/month the right range?
We expect 25M–45M tokens/month for Q4 ramp (current month is ~8M but we’re projecting growth). Low/high: 10M / 50M is safe for planning.

> - Latency SLO: interactive P95 < 300ms?
Yes — interactive must be snappy. For enrichment, latency is not critical but we want reasonable tails (<1s).

> - Continuous batching expectation: steady vs diurnal?
Enrichment is mostly steady during business hours (US day) and quieter overnight. Not perfectly uniform — expect an M-F pattern with peaks early morning and late-afternoon. So continuous batching is useful but there will be predictable peaks.

Target $/1M tokens
We’re targeting $40/1M tokens as a stretch goal, and $60/1M tokens as an acceptable ceiling. If you can show a path to $40 via batching + caching we’ll be excited.

Procurement contact
Looping in procurement (procurement@finbird.ai) for any contract-level questions.

We’re happy to run a 2-week canary. Please send the canary config and a short A/B plan.

—

Thanks Alyssa — perfect, that helps a lot. Confirming the key points we heard: 10M–50M planning band, stretch target $40/1M tokens, acceptable ceiling $60/1M tokens, enrichment is business-hour weighted with predictable peaks.

What we’ll deliver by tomorrow EOD (estimate + canary plan)
- Per-1M-token unit cost table for hosted continuous-batching vs. dedicated reserved capacity, showing impact of batching at low/typical/high volumes.
- Canary plan (2 weeks): run hosted continuous-batching with conservative batching window + KV prefix caching. Suggested config: batch window 10–20ms, worker concurrency cap 12, target P95 interactive <= 300ms (we’ll instrument). Expected cost delta: batching + cache -> ~12–18% lower unit cost for the enrichment profile you described vs. naive calls.
- Quick instructions for telemetry we’ll need (sample CSV attached earlier) and a minimal set of acceptance checks (latency, error-rate, token accuracy).

I’ve attached a short Markdown with the batching assumptions and a preliminary billing sheet. If procurement needs anything more formal we can produce an SOW.

Next sync: if the numbers look OK, can we schedule a 30-minute call on Monday to walk through the canary config and timelines? I’ll propose slots in the HubSpot deal.

Thanks again — we’ll send the estimate + canary config shortly.

Rishi
